text.p: A union representing TWA workers Monday warned the airline's board that it may go to court if the directors take any further steps to shrink the carrier.

In a statement, the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers (IAM) said it would be left with no choice but to go to court unless the board pledges to take no further action to make TWA smaller through layoffs, closings or asset sales, pending consideration of a purchase, merger or strategic alliance.

In a related move, the union, which represents more than 15,000 TWA employees, unanimously voted "no confidence" in Trans World Airlines Inc. interim Chief Executive Officer Gerald Gitner and called on him to step down in 60 days or less.
Gitner responded in a statement that he was "dismayed" by the union's stance and positions taken in its earlier letter, saying "it seriously misstates the plans and intentions" for TWA.
TWA spokesman John McDonald added that the union had always been fully aware of management's plans.
"The union is on the company's board," he said. "These actions are being taken by a board on which the union sits."
Gitner's letter to William O'Driscoll, president of Air Transport District Lodge 142, said the company's current strategy was "not to shrink TWA and certainly not to allow TWA to fail."
The letter did not directly address the "no confidence" vote or the call for Gitner to step down.

In another statement, William Scheri, general vice president of transportation for the union, said, "The answer here is a restructuring with new management, not further asset sales and massive layoffs of IAM members, flight attendants and pilots."
TWA spokesman McDonald said the layoffs the company announced in December as part of a plan to restructure its operations at John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York had taken place.

The machnists' union warned its members in January that TWA planned to lay off more than 700 people at Kennedy by Feb. 1. Union fight attendants were also told the carrier planned to lay off 195 workers at the airport last month.
TWA spent last week denying reports in USA Today that it had met with investor Brian Freeman, whose Strategic Capital Group reportedly proposed a deal to take control of the carrier.
Also last week, Transero, a Russian airline affiliated with Strategic Capital Group, also denied reports it was interested in taking control of TWA.
TWA shares closed down 18.75 cents Monday at $6.25.
